claims.text: Integrating CALPHAD thermodynamic simulations with machine-learning high-throughput screening can rapidly design intrinsically strong, ductile, and lightweight refractory HEAs.
Multi-principal-element refractory alloys have a broad composition space.
The baseline refractory alloy state exhibits complex phase mixtures.
HEAs exhibit lattice distortions because their constituent elements have different atomic sizes.
CALPHAD can assess phase stability and predict beneficial microstructural features in refractory HEAs.
Machine-learning algorithms can screen and optimize refractory HEA compositions for target properties.
High-performance alloys are relevant to high-temperature aerospace and energy applications.
The computational predictions will be validated through targeted experimental synthesis and testing.
A controlled single-phase or dual-phase microstructure, such as a BCC matrix with coherent precipitates, is a desirable structural state for the designed RHEAs.
A BCC-matrix precipitate microstructure can provide strengthening while preserving ductility and low density.
CALPHAD supplies phase-diagram and thermodynamic information that predicts desirable phases and lattice distortions.
Machine learning can correlate composition with mechanical properties in refractory HEAs.
Combining CALPHAD and machine learning quickly narrows the search space toward compositions with improved strength, ductility, and lower weight.
The proposed approach should yield RHEAs with strength greater than 2 GPa and ductility greater than 10%.
The proposed approach should yield alloys with lower density than conventionally designed alloys.
Traditional alloy-design paradigms commonly use one or two principal components rather than at least five.
Traditional alloy design relies on iterative trial-and-error experiments.
The method's success depends on the accuracy of CALPHAD databases for refractory systems.
The method's success depends on the quality and representativeness of the experimental data used to train the machine-learning models.
Exact property predictions are uncertain because refractory-alloy data are limited and simulation conditions may differ from real processing conditions.
